tldr: Thinking Machines Lab released open-weight looping models for local multimodal and reasoning research, while Signal introduced partial screen protections against operating-system AI agents.

New papers tackle training smaller models, sparse attention, speech event labeling and robot safety; international discussions about autonomous weapons and AI infrastructure remain proposals or negotiations, not settled safeguards, and all author benchmark claims need replication.

news.title: Thinking Machines Lab releases Apache-licensed Inkling 2 Mini
news.summary: Inkling 2 Mini is a 26.4B-parameter sparse MoE with 3.4B active parameters and three shared-layer loops per token. It accepts text/images, emits text and provides downloadable Apache-2.0 weights.
news.why_it_matters: A published low-bit checkpoint offers developers a local alternative for coding and tool-use research, with adjustable application integrations.
news.caveat: 5.4B effective activations per token are not equivalent to 5.4B unique weights; benchmark leadership, speed and 1M context are provider claims and workload-dependent. About 20GB checkpoint and at least 32GB GPU/unified memory are recommended.

news.title: Open variable-loop model enables studies of hidden reasoning and oversight
news.summary: Thinking Machines Lab published TML-d24-varloop-research, a 26.4B total-parameter multimodal research checkpoint allowing inference-time selection of shared-middle-layer passes.
news.why_it_matters: Holding weights fixed while changing loop count provides a controlled way to compare hidden computation, reasoning performance and chain-of-thought monitorability.
news.caveat: Only a research checkpoint, not a production API. Authors trained with 1–5 passes; generalization to more passes and no-CoT safety effects are not independently validated.

news.title: Signal adds screenshot defenses against operating-system AI agents
news.summary: Signal announced screen-capture restrictions on iOS 27 and selective Android AI-assistant capture checks to limit automated reading of private conversations.
news.why_it_matters: OS-integrated agents can cross app privacy boundaries even when message transport is encrypted; Signal is testing app-level mitigations.
news.caveat: Protections are incomplete, can be disabled and do not block all filesystem or OS-level access; Signal did not report that this announcement was a newly confirmed leak.

news.title: UN weapons talks commit to more autonomous-weapons negotiations through 2028
news.summary: Countries at Geneva Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons talks agreed to continue negotiating autonomous-weapons rules within two years, Reuters reported November 21 UTC.
news.why_it_matters: Human control of lethal decisions remains an international governance issue as increasingly autonomous targeting tools proliferate.
news.caveat: No binding global ban or substantive treaty was adopted; the U.S., Russia and Israel opposed the requested binding rules, and consensus language remains limited.

news.title: US Treasury chief says Washington and Beijing backed human oversight of military AI
news.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that Trump and Xi agreed humans should be involved in major military decisions supported by AI, Reuters reported.
news.why_it_matters: An attributed bilateral position may affect expectations for human involvement in military AI, separate from multilateral treaty negotiations.
news.caveat: This is one official's description of an agreement, not a published, independently verified, binding treaty or deployed safeguard.

news.title: US president threatens penalties for American companies building data centers abroad
news.summary: President Trump said his administration would penalize U.S. companies that build overseas data centers, suggesting a large tax; Reuters reported the remarks from a press conference.
news.why_it_matters: A future policy could materially change regional AI capacity planning, latency, and foreign investment decisions.
news.caveat: A public threat is not an enacted law, published tax rule or proof penalties have been imposed; key implementation details remain unknown.

news.title: AutoMaster paper uses skill-guided rollouts to improve post-training of small models
news.summary: AutoMaster generates behavior-focused skill instructions to shape teacher trajectories before SFT, reporting gains of 1.42–8.99 percentage points over a controlled baseline on 4B/9B coding, search and terminal tasks.
news.why_it_matters: Targets better synthetic training demonstrations rather than simply buying more teacher calls or model scale.
news.caveat: Preprint, author-selected benchmarks and no independent replication; skill instruction leakage and broader task transfer require study.

news.title: HiSA research sparsifies attention feature dimensions instead of tokens
news.summary: Hidden Sparse Attention omits selected RoPE query-key feature-product components, reporting about one-third of the dot-product terms in tested settings and FlashAttention-3 integration.
news.why_it_matters: Feature-axis sparsity offers a different computational tradeoff from token pruning or sliding-window attention.
news.caveat: Training from scratch and custom kernels limit drop-in adoption; author-measured accuracy, memory and speed have not been independently replicated.

news.title: dLoop explores more computation before diffusion-language token commitment
news.summary: The dLoop preprint adds repeated parameter-shared middle-block processing of a partially masked sequence before committing generated tokens, and reports favorable accuracy/throughput tradeoffs on selected tasks.
news.why_it_matters: Refinement loops may reduce errors in parallel token generation without only changing confidence thresholds.
news.caveat: Authors report mixed throughput comparisons depending on baseline and accounting for repeated passes; results are not a general speed guarantee.

news.title: Multi-turn safeguarding study finds risks missed when warning cues appear gradually
news.summary: A research preprint using nine scenarios and over 7,400 simulated conversations reports that several assistants met community-worker safeguarding criteria less often when subtle risk cues were dispersed across turns.
news.why_it_matters: Tests whether safety evaluations built around one obvious message overstate performance in longer, realistic conversations.
news.caveat: Scenario judgments are from three support workers; synthetic interactions, model versions and prompts constrain generalization. These are findings, not a confirmed individual-user incident.

news.title: Xing-Audio study combines speech transcripts and six classes of vocal sounds
news.summary: Authors describe a 1.7B-parameter model trained with about 800,000 cross-audited/mined utterances to label speech alongside non-verbal vocalizations such as breathing.
news.why_it_matters: Unified recognition could preserve communication cues that conventional speech-to-text systems omit.
news.caveat: Author benchmarks only; weights, inference code, dataset and evaluation artifacts are described as planned for release, not currently verified available.

news.title: AgentRoboCritic analyzes action-by-action robot-control failures
news.summary: Researchers introduce intent-grounded critiques across 12 robot-manipulation benchmarks with 12,844 labeled actions; they report a fine-tuned critic improves failure-mode accuracy in their human-annotated test.
news.why_it_matters: Action-level diagnosis can reveal grasping, alignment and recovery weaknesses hidden by episode pass rates.
news.caveat: The disclosed benchmark and fine-tuned critic do not establish safe or robust physical deployment; reported performance is from a research test, not independent field validation.

news.title: SAFI trains vision-language-action robots to halt prohibited tasks mid-execution
news.summary: State-Aware Fallback Imitation (SAFI) trains a policy to hold a safe stationary arm and gripper state when takeover occurs after a forbidden task has already started, tested on LIBERO/BadLIBERO.
news.why_it_matters: A refusal at task start alone is insufficient when a robot is already moving or holding an object.
news.caveat: The 1.3% prohibited-completion result and lack of recorded physical incidents apply only to evaluated setups; do not infer guaranteed real-world safety.

news.title: Anytime-valid testing paper formalizes when an AI answer sampler may stop
news.summary: Researchers propose reward-weighted answer clustering and an e-process-based stopping rule that can certify sampled majority answers under stated statistical assumptions.
news.why_it_matters: Variable per-query sample budgets could cut unnecessary best-of-N inference while bounding a specific premature-certification error.
news.caveat: A certified answer majority is not a guarantee of factual correctness; sequential validity depends on distributional assumptions and the reported cost gains are author-evaluated.
